article_text:
“The Witcher” and “Planet of the Apes” star Freya Allan is set to star in “System,” the upcoming horror film from Norwegian director Joachim Rønning .

Plot details remain under wraps, but production is currently underway on location in the old, abandoned underground stations and tunnels under London. Freya will be joined by Denzel Baidoo (“Last Swim”) and Felix Edwards (“MobLand”) in supporting roles.

Related Stories

'Kefi' Review: A Grief-Stricken Family Reunion Is Beset by Aliens, Drugs and Dinosaurs in Kisin Saito's Kaleidoscopic, Genre-Fluid Debut

Netflix Docuseries 'The One About Matthew Perry' Is a Tragic, Mournful Portrait of Addiction: TV Review

Rønning, who broke out with “Kon-Tiki” and would go on to direct major franchise titles including “Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales” and the recent “Tron: Ares,” will write, direct, and produce for The Saga Company. He penned the screenplay with his brother, Andreas Rønning.

Roy Lee (“Weapons,” “It,” “The Ring”) and Steven Schneider (“Paranormal Activity,” “Insidious,” “Pet Sematary”) will produce for Spooky Pictures. Stewart le Maréchal and Anna Mohr-Pietsch produce for MetFilm. Image Nation Studios’ CEO Ben Ross (“Watcher,” “Company”), Spooky Pictures’ Rami Yasin (“Hokum”), and Andreas Rønning will executive produce.

UTA Independent Film Group arranged the financing and is representing the film’s sale.

Under the Spooky Pictures-Image Nation Studios partnership, the companies have produced genre projects including “Late Night with the Devil,” Charlie Polinger’s “The Plague,” “Hokum” starring Adam Scott, Casey Affleck’s “Company” and Guy Nattiv’s “The Liberation.”

Allan is perhaps best known for her role as Ciri, in Netflix’s global phenomenon “The Witcher,” a performance that earned her two Saturn Award nominations. She will return to her role for the fifth and final season, which is expected to release in late 2027. She recently finished shooting Nick Hamm’s |Black Palace” for Tempo Productions. Freya also was seen leading Wes Ball’s “Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes,” the fourth instalment in the Planet of the Apes reboot series, with her acclaimed performance landing her a slot on Variety ’s Power of Young Hollywood Impact Report in 2024.

She is represented by CAA, United Agents, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman Wertheimer Mandelbaum Morris Bernstein Trattner Auerbach Hynick Jaime LeVine Sample & Klein. Rønning is represented by UTA and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern.

article_text:
Films and events

Debate

I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning

In Clio Barnard’s poignant drama, five childhood friends from Birmingham find their lifelong bonds tested as adulthood brings fractured relationships, unfulfilled dreams and long-buried secrets to light.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Clio Barnard

Screenwriter Enda Walsh

With Anthony Boyle, Daryl McCormack, Jay Lycurgo, Lola Petticrew, Joe Cole

UK 2026. 110min

Courtesy of Curzon Film

Language English

In association with

Access information

Friday 16 October 20:40

Audio description

Sunday 18 October 11:30

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Sunday 18 October 12:00

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Adapted from Kieran Goddard’s novel, this intoxicating yet compassionate film by the director of The Selfish Giant and Ali & Ava is propelled by a superb ensemble cast and the euphoric pulse of club music. As moments of youthful joy gradually give way to disillusionment, the film offers a piercing portrait of contemporary Britain, exposing exploitative social structures and widening inequality as forces that have deeply marked its characters’ lives.

Hyun Jin Cho

Content advice

Contains flashing images.

Contains scenes of domestic violence or abuse, drug use, graphic violence or injury, harm towards children, sex, and suicide.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Lemonade

Barry Keoghan plays a social worker trying to make up for the past in this heartfelt coming-of-age Irish drama about second chances.

Tender Loving Care

In a world that feels increasingly untethered from human connection, the incomparable Mike Leigh returns with a thought-provoking and compassionate view of urban life.

Club Kid

A jaded New York club promoter finds his messy lifestyle upended by the discovery that he has a son, in Jordan Firstman’s hilarious feature directorial debut.

article_text:
Del 3 al 4 de octubre, Artishock participa en Feria Aparte con una selección de fotografía latinoamericana y obras de pequeño formato de artistas chilenos. Una nueva ocasión para llevar al espacio físico las conversaciones que, desde hace más de 15 años, desarrollamos principalmente desde nuestra plataforma digital.

Desde 2010, Artishock ha construido un lugar para el arte contemporáneo latino/ibero/americano desde Santiago de Chile. Durante todos estos años, gran parte de nuestros encuentros han ocurrido en nuestra plataforma online, a través de entrevistas, reseñas y ensayos que involucran a una amplia comunidad de artistas, curadores, directores de museos y proyectos independientes.

Pero la historia de Artishock también se cuenta desde algunos momentos fuera de la pantalla. Entre el 3 y el 4 de octubre volvemos a ese espacio presencial de la mano de Feria Aparte , con una propuesta que pone en relación dos conjuntos de obras que acercan prácticas y geografías que no siempre tienen la posibilidad de encontrarse físicamente.

El primero reúne fotografía latinoamericana , seleccionada a partir de una convocatoria abierta en la que participaron artistas de Chile, Venezuela, Colombia, México, Cuba, Argentina, Perú y Ecuador. Son trabajos que se acercan de distintas maneras al paisaje, el cuerpo y la vida cotidiana, y que permiten recorrer imaginarios diversos de la región sin reducirlos a una única mirada sobre lo latinoamericano.

Entre las obras seleccionadas se encuentran fotografías de Alexandra Busch, Carelyn Mejías, Diego Barriga, Edgar Martínez, Fernando Izaguirre, Frank Lahera, Gabriela de Echave, Joaquín Rodríguez, José Antonio Barrientos, Joseph Ladrón de Guevara, Lucía Pizzani, Misha Vallejo, Nicolás Rivas, Rafael Triana, Sebastián González y Valeria Arendar .

El segundo conjunto está compuesto por esculturas y objetos de pequeño formato realizados por artistas chilenos y chilenas . Cerámica, vidrio, cartón y otros materiales orgánicos e industriales configuran piezas que se mueven entre lo cotidiano y lo extraño.

Participan Borja Carbajal, Constanza Hermosilla, Daniela Pulido, Elizabeth Burmann Littin, Inés González, Isidora Kauak, Jessica Briceño, José Esteban Valdés, Las Honorarias, Martín Vásquez & Violeta Cereceda y Rocío Olivares .

En esta curaduría encontrarás obras de distintas escalas y rangos de precio, pensadas también como una manera de acercarse al coleccionismo de arte contemporáneo. Las obras estarán disponibles para la venta durante la feria y pueden consultarse tanto en nuestro catálogo online como en Artishop.

[Ver catálogo completo en PDF – Precios en pesos chilenos] [Ver obras disponibles en Artishop – Precios en dólares]

Del archivo digital al encuentro presencial

Participar en Feria Aparte significa para Artishock algo más que incorporar una dimensión comercial a nuestro trabajo. Después de más de quince años construyendo un archivo digital dedicado al arte contemporáneo de la región, estar frente a las obras, conversar con quienes las hacen y conocer nuevos públicos es también una manera de poner en práctica aquello que ha guiado nuestro trabajo desde el comienzo: conectar escenas y comunidades que están cultural y geográficamente cerca, pero que no siempre tienen oportunidades de encontrarse.

Por eso, esta participación también marca un pequeño cambio de escala para nosotros. Artishock nació en Santiago, pero su comunidad se ha extendido mucho más allá de esta ciudad y de Chile. Llevar a Feria Aparte una selección latinoamericana y, al mismo tiempo, compartir el trabajo de artistas que desarrollan sus prácticas en Chile, nos permite poner esas distintas escenas en relación dentro de un mismo espacio.

A esta participación se suma el Premio Artishock , que reconocerá a uno/a de los/as artistas participantes de Feria Aparte con un perfil dedicado a su trabajo en nuestra plataforma. La iniciativa busca que el encuentro no termine cuando cierre la feria: la obra y la práctica de ese/a artista continuarán circulando en el archivo digital de Artishock.

El arte es por acá

La quinta edición de Feria Aparte reunirá a 40 expositores para un total de más 200 artistas en la Ex Cervecería Ebner, edificio patrimonial ubicado en el Mall Barrio Independencia. La programación incluye conversatorios, talleres, música en vivo, recorridos y actividades de mediación, además de la exposición y venta de obras.

Para Artishock, estar aquí es también una manera de volver a casa: encontrarnos en la ciudad donde nació la plataforma, pero hacerlo ahora de otra forma, alrededor de obras, artistas y conversaciones compartidas.

¡ Los esperamos del 3 al 4 de octubre en Feria Aparte!

"我们常常想象记忆是线性的、整洁的、按时间顺序排列的，甚至是听话的。它在被召唤时出现，化为叙事，并将我们整齐地安置在各自的历史之中。在《记忆的形状》（The Shape of Memory）中，当代视觉艺术家杰西卡·阿朱亚（Jessica Ajuyah）彻底挑战了这一假设，创作了一组拒绝将记忆定格的作品，转而任由其“含糊不清”、不明朗且支离破碎，其受到的遗忘和重新诠释的影响，绝不亚于回忆本身。", true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在阿朱亚的世界里，铭记不只是回首过去；它是一种重建、重新诠释，并在许多方面是一种成型。这一点在“Orjogun”中体现得淋漓尽致——这是一个意为“战士”的伊齐克里语（Itsekiri）词汇。处于画面正中的人物带有明显的挣扎痕迹：深深的面部疤痕、流血的鼻子。然而，这里没有任何失败感。若说有什么不同，那就是该作品抗拒将痛苦戏剧化，转而将韧性重新构筑为循环往复、持续不断的过程——即不断“拍掉身上灰尘”的无声举动。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Jessica2-300x210.jpg", "alt": "Jessica2", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种对力量的重新诠释延伸到了《无声遐想》（Silent Reverie）中，其中的反叛呈现出更安静、更内敛的形式。在这里，抵抗并不喧闹、不具对抗性，而是极具个人色彩——这是对自身选择的一种简单而激进的践行。这件作品指向了一种常常被忽视的自主性：在那些并不轻易允许它的空间中，自我定义的权力。它提醒我们，行动力并不总是大声宣告；有时，它是在沉默中度过的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Jessica3-300x210.png", "alt": "Jessica3", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《绿色中的蛹》（Chrysalis in Green）中，阿朱亚对女性特质的探讨变得更加富有层次。这件作品创作于她自己的人生中充满围绕婚姻和母亲身份的社会期望的时期，它以一种保持距离的方式探讨母爱——这是一种想象中的亲密感，而非亲历的亲密感。这里有一种温柔，但也有着一股暗流涌动的张力，尤其是构图中所暗示的代际动态。该作品表明，这种爱并非没有期望；它正是由期望塑造的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Jessica4-300x200.jpg", "alt": "Jessica4", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《乡愁》（Homesick）延续了个人经历与更广泛文化叙事之间的这种互动。在这里，归属感概念扎根于诸如食物或对话这样极为亲密的事物中。这件作品触及了一种极其熟悉的感觉；那种在缺席时最为强烈地涌现的对家的渴望。从这个意义上说，文化身份并非抽象的；它是感官的、具身的，并且往往与日常生活仪式紧密相连。害羞（homesick）不仅是思念一个地方，更是思念那个存在于其中的自己。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Jessica5-300x300.jpg", "alt": "Jessica5", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如果说渴望是向后看的，那么《流动的自我》（Fluid Self）则转向外部，拥抱改变的可能性。身份变得松动、扩展，并拒绝被局限。对阿朱亚而言，这种拒绝中蕴含着一种自由感；她认识到自我不必一成不变，而是可以随着经验做出调整。这或许是展览中最具解放意义的主张之一：一个人可以同时拥有许多身份，而这种多元性并非缺点，而是一种力量。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在视觉上，阿朱亚通过经过深思熟虑的形式与母题语言强化了这些理念。花卉在整个展览中反复出现，不仅作为装饰元素，更作为成长和转化的象征。它们在不同阶段绽放，表明成长的过程并非千篇一律或整齐划一。每个人都按自己的节奏前行，并由各自的处境所塑造。同样，无面孔人物的使用将焦点从个体身份上移开，为它们留出了诠释的空间。这是对观者在作品中寻找自我的一种邀请。其结果是一种既有深度个人体验又具广泛共鸣的观展感受。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些作品构成了展览中更广泛探索的一部分，在此过程中，阿朱亚以多样且细腻的方式不断回归记忆、身份和转型。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《记忆的形状》区别于阿朱亚早期作品的地方，在于它拥抱了脆弱性，并甘愿保持未完成的状态。在其核心，展览回归到一个核心问题：当记忆本身并不可靠时，我们究竟是谁？阿朱亚没有给出直接的答案；相反，她让作品在其流动性中存在，将不确定性视为过程的一部分，这种方法标志着从早期更具结构性的作品向更具直觉性的创作的转变。这是一种远离控制、走向探索的运动——对“不知”保持开放，让意义自然涌现，而不是从一开始就对其进行定义。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在整个展览中，人们也能感受到对其所处更广阔环境的意识。对于女性创作者，尤其是身为有色女性的创作者而言，自我定义的过程往往因结构性局限和期望而变得错综复杂。尽管在为这些声音创造空间方面取得了进展，但差距依然存在。阿朱亚的作品并未直接解决这些状况，但它在这些空间中的存在本身，就凸显了“在场”的重要性：即创作那些坚持被看见的作品，即便是在仍在演变的系统中亦是如此说不定也是如此的坚持不懈（注：顺应上下文风格，译为“即便是在仍在演变的系统中也是如此”）。作品强调了在场的重要性：创作出坚持被看见的作品，哪怕是在那些仍在演变的系统之中亦是如此（依最终输出核对）。原文：its very existence within these spaces underscores the importance of presence: of creating work that insists on being seen, even within systems that are still evolving. article_text:
Her work situates her within a new generation of artists engaging memory, identity, and selfhood with nuance and introspection. It is a trajectory that signals both clarity of vision and an openness to evolution.

The Shape of Memory: Jessica Ajuyah on Transformation, Womanhood and the Fluid-Self

A deeply personal yet universally resonant exploration of how we remember, reshape and reclaim ourselves.

Memory as we often imagine it is linear, tidy, chronological, and even obedient. It arrives when called, resolves itself into narrative, and situates us neatly within our own histories. In The Shape of Memory , contemporary visual artist Jessica Ajuyah challenges this assumption entirely, creating a body of work that refuses to fix memory in place, instead allowing it to be “mumbled,” unclear and fragmented, shaped as much by omission and reinterpretation as by recollection itself.

In Ajuyah’s world, to remember is not simply to look back; it is to reconstruct, reinterpret, and in many ways, to become. Nowhere is this more evident than in ‘ Orjogun ’–an Itsekiri word for “warrior.” The figure at its center bears visible signs of struggle: a deep facial scar, a bleeding nose. Yet there is no sense of defeat. If anything, the work resists the dramatization of pain, instead reframing resilience as cyclical and ongoing–the quiet act of continually ‘dusting oneself off.’

This reframing of strength extends into ‘ Silent Reverie ,’ where rebellion takes on a quieter, more interior form. Here, resistance is not loud or confrontational but deeply personal–the simple, radical act of inhabiting one’s own choices. The work gestures toward a kind of autonomy that is often overlooked: the power of self-definition in spaces that do not readily allow for it. It is a reminder that agency does not always announce itself; sometimes, it is lived in silence.

Ajuyah’s exploration of womanhood becomes even more layered in ‘Chrysalis in Green .’ Created during a period marked by societal expectations around marriage and motherhood in her own life, the piece approaches maternal love from a distance–an imagined intimacy rather than a lived one. There is a tenderness here, but also an undercurrent of tension, particularly in the generational dynamics hinted at within the composition. The work suggests that this love is not free from expectation; it is shaped by it.

‘ Homesick ’ continues that interplay between personal experience and broader cultural narratives. Here the concept of belonging is anchored in something as intimate as food or dialogue. The work taps into a deeply familiar sensation; the longing for home that emerges most acutely in its absence. Cultural identity, in this sense, is not abstract; it is sensory, embodied, and often tied to the rituals of everyday life. To be homesick is not simply to miss a place, but to miss the version of oneself that exists within it.

If longing looks backward, ‘Fluid Self ’ turns outward, embracing the possibility of change. Identity loosens, expands, and refuses containment. For Ajuyah, there is a sense of freedom in this refusal; recognition that the self does not have to remain fixed, but instead it can shift in response to experience. It is perhaps one of the exhibition’s most liberating propositions: that one can be many things at once, and that this plurality is not a flaw but a strength.

Visually, Ajuyah reinforces these ideas through a carefully considered language of form and motif. Florals recur throughout the exhibition, not merely as decorative elements but as symbols of growth and transformation. They bloom at different stages, suggesting that becoming is not uniform or synchronized. Each individual moves at their own pace, shaped by their own circumstances. Similarly, the use of faceless figures shifts the focus away from individual identity, opening them up to interpretation. An invitation for the viewer to see themselves within the work. The result is an experience that feels both deeply personal and broadly resonant.

These works form part of a wider exploration within the exhibition, where Ajuyah continues to return to memory, identity, and transformation in varied and nuanced ways.

What distinguishes The Shape of Memory from Ajuyah’s earlier work is its embrace of vulnerability and willingness to remain unresolved. At its core, the exhibition returns to a central question: who are we when memory itself is unreliable? Ajuyah offers no direct answers; instead, allowing the work to exist in its fluidity, embracing uncertainty as part of the process, an approach that marks a shift from earlier, more structured work into something more intuitive. It is a movement away from control and toward exploration–an openness to not knowing, to allowing meaning to emerge rather than defining it from the outset.

There is also an awareness, throughout the exhibition, of the broader landscape in which it exists. For women creatives, particularly women of color, the act of self-definition is often complicated by structural limitations and expectations. While progress has been made in creating spaces for these voices, gaps remain. Ajuyah’s work does not directly address these conditions, but its very existence within these spaces underscores the importance of presence: of creating work that insists on being seen, even within systems that are still evolving.

Ultimately, The Shape of Memory unfolds as an inquiry into how we come to understand ourselves–how we choose what to hold onto, what to reshape, and how we might allow ourselves the freedom to exist beyond fixed definitions of identity, culture, and expectation. To engage with this work is to be reminded that memory is not something we simply possess, but something we continuously make. And in that making, we too are transformed.

What emerges is a practice that feels both deeply considered and still in the process of becoming. As Ajuyah continues to refine her visual language, her work situates her within a new generation of artists engaging memory, identity, and selfhood with nuance and introspection. It is a trajectory that signals both clarity of vision and an openness to evolution.

article_text:
November means fall is in full swing, and Netflix has a ton of new titles to celebrate. Whether you’re looking to watch family-friendly films over Thanksgiving or are still looking to be spooked post-spooky season, there is something, new or old, for everyone.

One highly anticipated film joining the streamer this month is “The Mosquito Bowl” starring Nicholas Galitzine, Bill Skarsgård, Peter Berg and more. The film follows four college football stars in the aftermath of Pearl Harbor as they enlist in the US Marines, discovering the strength of brotherhood and the cost of war.

article_text:
M y love of African animals, in particular elephants, dates back to when I was three or four years old, growing up in Milan in a house full of old nature books. When I was six, my parents took me on my first safari in Kenya – I cried on the plane home, feeling I was being torn away from the savanna I’d dreamed of, somewhere I really loved. But for the past 20 years, that’s where I’ve lived, guiding photographers on the Maasai Mara National Reserve and elsewhere in Africa.

I’ve spent time photographing other animals, especially big cats, but elephants are still my favourite subject. They have this extraordinary presence, dominating the landscape and making it come alive. I love to follow them in different habitats. They are extremely adaptable – in Kenya they’re associated with the savanna and acacia woodland, and they can also live in extremely arid areas, such as the deserts of Namibia, where this photograph was taken.

I was there last September, guiding a group of photographers. We had been following a group of elephants walking along a dry riverbed as night fell. Even though there is no water in these rivers, they retain some vegetation and act as a lifeline for the elephants, who follow them from the hills in the west towards the Atlantic Ocean.

Because it’s a sandy river, it was quite easy to follow their tracks until we found them again the next day. But among the tracks was something quite unusual, like a dragging mark. Sometimes bull elephants, when they’re full of testosterone, will do crazy things to demonstrate their power and intimidate their opponents – I’d seen one lift a log before, and thought perhaps that’s what was being dragged.

We drove on until we found them, and that’s when I realised one of the females was carrying a baby. When people see this picture, they sometimes think it’s of a young elephant hugging its mother, but in fact the calf is dead and the leg you can’t see is wedged between the adult’s tusk and trunk. As I took this photograph, another elephant was approaching and the female swung her head so the baby was lifted up and out of its way. I have other photographs that make the reading of the scene more straightforward, but this one leaves the interpretation open and adds a layer of mystery.

We followed the herd for several hours, and the female carried the calf for the entire time, only putting it down so she could feed before picking it up and continuing on her way. She was still carrying it when we last saw her – eventually the elephants started climbing into some rocky hills where we couldn’t follow.

I’ve since read that 17 out of the 19 calves born in that area during the past four years have not made it. There’s clearly a problem, but researchers aren’t yet clear why this is happening. What has come to light, however, is that the elephant carrying the calf was not its mother, as I had assumed. Her mammary glands were not swollen as they would have been if she’d recently given birth, and the researchers were able to identify her as a female who had a miscarriage a couple of years before, and had since been seen picking up the stillborn calves of other mothers. In a sense, that makes the image even more deep and profound, as it implies that she perhaps hasn’t moved past that trauma.

Most of my elephant photographs are in black and white. Sometimes I use colour – in Tsavo, Kenya, elephants are often covered in red earth, which makes for a striking contrast against green vegetation, and in Etosha, Namibia, there’s a place where they visit a waterhole full of white clay and end up looking like ghosts. But black and white highlights the texture of elephants’ skin, and also, as here, removes distracting elements and exposes emotion in a more straightforward way.

This is a painful image to look at, but at the same time it reveals so much of the psychology of elephants, their interior complexity, personality and feelings. Here we see a creature that feels just as much as we do, that experiences the same grief at losing a baby, the same sense of not wanting to let it go. My hope is that photographs like this help people realise how important it is to coexist peacefully and respectfully with animals that look different to us on the outside, but inside are very similar.

This image is the adult grand title winner of Wildlife Photographer of the Year. The exhibition is at the Natural History Museum, London, until 11 July 2027.

{"type": "paragraph", "text": "冯·赖丁斯沃德曾在新罕布什尔大学和位于科勒尔盖布尔斯的迈阿密大学学习，并获得了学士和硕士学位。随后，她与第一任丈夫米尔顿·冯·赖丁斯沃德（Milton von Rydingsvard）一起搬到了加利福尼亚州奥克兰，并育有一女乌苏拉·安妮（Ursula Anne）。她在1973年与他离婚，并带着女儿搬到纽约，进入哥伦比亚大学深造，师从马克斯·科兹洛夫（Max Kozloff）、迈耶·夏皮罗（Meyer Schapiro）和乔治·舒加曼（George Sugarman），并于1975年获得美术硕士学位。离开哥大后，她在苏荷区买下了一处阁楼，并于1981年将工作室搬到了布鲁克林，她的余生职业生涯皆在此度过。1985年，她与诺贝尔奖得主神经科学家保罗·格林加德（Paul Greengard）结婚，后者于2019年去世。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在其职业生涯的早期，冯·赖丁斯沃德也曾涉足绘画和钢材创作，直到她发现木材是最适合其探索的材料。雪松是通过画家迈克尔·穆尔赫恩（Michael Mulhern）来到冯·赖丁斯沃德手里的，后者为她购买了许多4×4规格的木梁。随后，她将这些木头带到了一家金属加工车间并开始切割，沉迷于自己如何能从中获得“看起来像泥土，或者看起来充满肉感的形式”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/images-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "雪松与雕塑的形式", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此，木材随着时间成为了冯·赖丁斯沃德的标志。她使用标准尺寸的雪松木梁，将其切割并组装成复杂的结构，随后再用圆锯和其他工具进行加工。由此产生的表面——布满了沟槽、凸起和刻痕——保留了建造过程的痕迹，区块最初的规则性被彻底改变，直至产生出看似属于某种不同于建筑或工业秩序的体量。她的作品有时让人联想起巨大的容器、墙壁、器皿和风景碎片，却从未固定在单一的表征上；纪念碑式的宏大尺度与细致入微的加工共存，而抽象则让与身体和有机形态的联想浮出水面。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在她最著名的作品中包括《Ona》（2013年），这是一件永久安装在布鲁克林巴克莱中心室外的青铜雕塑。该作品高约6米，其形态最初通过对雪松的加工开发出来，随后被转化为青铜。该标题在波兰语中意为“她”，伴随着一个表面呈波浪状、向上扩大的结构。“我非常希望人们去触摸它，”她在作品落成之际向《纽约时报》说道。“手指上的酸液会使其发光，就像人们揉搓佛陀的肚子一样。”", "links": [{"text": "dichiarato al New York Times", "url": "https://www.nytimes.com/2013/08/31/arts/design/ona-by-ursula-von-rydingsvard-arrives-in-brooklyn.html"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "超越木材", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管雪松仍然是与其名字最紧密联系的材料，但冯·赖丁斯瓦德也曾使用青铜、树脂、织物、纸张以及不太常规的材料进行创作，这些材料同样没有改变其研究的核心，即构建保留了物理维度和某种具象模糊性的形态。她的作品已被纽约现代艺术博物馆、大都会艺术博物馆和惠特尼美国艺术博物馆等机构的收藏所收录，而她的个展则曾由费城艺术博物馆和英国约克郡雕塑公园等机构主办。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/GL-9252-Bronze-Bowl-with-Lace-1_uvr1-683x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Ursula von Rydingsvard, Bronze Bowl with Lace, 2013-14. © Ursula von Rydingsvard. Credits: the artist and Galerie Lelong. Photo: Jonty Wilde", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此，在冯·赖丁斯瓦德的作品中，记忆并非作为生平故事的图解呈现，而是作为一种间接的存在，寄托于材料的选择和形态的构建之中。她的雕塑在沉重与脆弱之间、在体量的高大与有机材料的脆弱性之间保持着一种张力。正是在这种平衡中，以及通过强化加工过程将普通材料转化的可能性里，人们得以辨认出她研究的独特性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "冯·赖丁斯瓦德非常厌恶极简主义的理论方法和冰冷敏感性，以至于她曾对策展人马克·罗森塔尔（Mark Rosenthal）——后者于2018年在费城的织物工坊与博物馆（Fabric Workshop and Museum）为她组织了一场展览——说过：“那里没有感官性，也没有人性。”", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Ursula von Rydingsvard , scultrice e tra le voci più riconoscibili della scena artistica statunitense, è morta il 27 ottobre 2026 nella sua casa di Manhattan, all’età di 84 anni. La responsabile dello studio dell’artista, Courtney Childress , ha attribuito la morte di Von Rydingsvard al morbo di Alzheimer, secondo quanto riportato dal New York Times .

La Galerie Lelong , che ha rappresentato von Rydingsvard negli ultimi trent’anni, ha annunciato la scomparsa con queste parole: «Nonostante gli enormi ostacoli, Ursula possedeva una spinta inimitabile a creare e a trasformare immagini pressoché inimmaginabili in opere di dimensioni monumentali». Mary Sabbatino , vicepresidente della galleria, ha aggiunto nel comunicato: «Le sue sculture si ergono come sentinelle per ispirare le nuove generazioni, in particolare le scultrici, a sognare nuove possibilità».

Nel corso di oltre cinquant’anni di attività, von Rydingsvard ha sviluppato una ricerca incentrata sulle possibilità espressive del legno, realizzando sculture monumentali in cui la lavorazione della materia produce forme irregolari, vicine tanto alle strutture naturali quanto agli oggetti d’uso quotidiano.

Visualizza questo post su Instagram Un post condiviso da Galerie Lelong (@galerielelong)

Nel corso della sua carriera ultra cinquantennale, enormi travi di cedro sono state plasmate in una varietà di sculture imponenti, ma anche bronzo, tessuti e intestini animali sono stati ambiti di indagine fecondi. «Era come il sole. Era una forza che attirava le persone e le teneva in orbita attorno a sé», ha dichiarato Childress durante un’intervista telefonica alla testata Hyperallergic . «Si muoveva per lo studio come se avesse i capelli in fiamme e non riusciva mai a rallentare».

Chi era Ursula von Rydingsvard

Nata nel 1942 a Deensen, in Germania, da madre polacca e padre ucraino, l’artista ha trascorso l’infanzia tra campi di lavoro e campi profughi, prima di trasferirsi con la famiglia negli Stati Uniti nel 1950. Un’esperienza segnata dallo sradicamento e dalla precarietà che avrebbe costituito uno dei riferimenti per la sua ricerca, pur senza tradursi in un racconto autobiografico diretto. Le immagini delle baracche di legno e degli oggetti essenziali della vita quotidiana sarebbero infatti riemerse nel suo lavoro attraverso forme ambigue, sospese tra memoria personale e astrazione.

Von Rydingsvard studiò all’Università del New Hampshire e all’Università di Miami, a Coral Gables, conseguendo una laurea e un master. Si trasferì poi a Oakland, in California, con il suo primo marito, Milton von Rydingsvard , dal quale ebbe una figlia, Ursula Anne. Divorziò da lui nel 1973 e si trasferì con la figlia a New York, iscrivendosi alla Columbia University, dove studiò con Max Kozloff , Meyer Schapiro e George Sugarman , conseguendo un master in belle arti nel 1975. Dopo la Columbia, acquistò un loft a SoHo e nel 1981 trasferì il suo studio a Brooklyn, dove rimase per il resto della sua carriera. Nel 1985 sposò il neuroscienziato premio Nobel Paul Greengard , scomparso nel 2019.

Nei primi anni della sua carriera, v on Rydingsvard ha lavorato anche con la pittura e l’acciaio, prima di individuare nel legno il materiale più adatto alla sua ricerca. Il cedro arrivò a von Rydingsvard tramite il pittore Michael Mulhern, che le acquistò molti travi 4×4. In seguito, lei portò il legno in un laboratorio di lavorazione dei metalli e iniziò a tagliarlo, dilettandosi nel modo in cui riusciva a ottenere «forme che sembravano terra, o che sembravano carnose».

Il cedro e le forme della scultura

Il legno è quindi diventato col tempo la firma di Von Rydingsvard, che utilizzava travi di cedro di dimensioni standard, tagliandole e assemblandole in strutture complesse, successivamente lavorate con seghe circolari e altri strumenti. Le superfici risultanti – percorse da solchi, sporgenze e incisioni – conservano la traccia del processo di costruzione, e la regolarità iniziale dei blocchi viene irrimediabilmente alterata fino a generare volumi che sembrano appartenere a un ordine diverso da quello architettonico o industriale. Le sue opere richiamano talvolta grandi recipienti, pareti, utensili e frammenti di paesaggio, senza mai fissarsi in una rappresentazione univoca; la scala monumentale convive con una lavorazione minuziosa, mentre l’astrazione lascia affiorare associazioni con il corpo e con le forme organiche.

Tra le opere più note figura Ona (2013), scultura in bronzo installata permanentemente all’esterno del Barclays Center di Brooklyn. Alta circa sei metri, l’opera deriva da una forma originariamente sviluppata attraverso la lavorazione del cedro e successivamente tradotta in bronzo. Il titolo significa “lei” in polacco e accompagna una struttura dalla superficie ondulata, che si allarga verso l’alto. « Mi piacerebbe molto che le persone la toccassero», ha dichiarato al New York Times in occasione dell’inaugurazione dell’opera . «L’acido delle dita la lucida, come quando ai Buddha viene massaggiata la pancia».

Oltre il legno

Sebbene il cedro sia rimasto il materiale associato più immediatamente al suo nome, von Rydingsvard ha lavorato anche con bronzo, resina, tessuti, carta e materiali meno convenzionali, che pure non hanno modificato il nucleo della sua ricerca, legato alla costruzione di forme che conservano una dimensione fisica e una certa ambiguità figurativa. Le opere sono entrate nelle collezioni di istituzioni come il Museum of Modern Art, il Metropolitan Museum of Art e il Whitney Museum of American Art di New York, mentre le sue mostre personali sono state ospitate, tra gli altri, dal Philadelphia Museum of Art e dallo Yorkshire Sculpture Park nel Regno Unito.

Nel lavoro di von Rydingsvard, la memoria non si presenta dunque come illustrazione di una vicenda biografica, ma come una presenza indiretta, affidata alla scelta dei materiali e alla costruzione delle forme. Le sculture mantengono una tensione tra peso e fragilità, tra l’imponenza del volume e la vulnerabilità della materia organica. È in questo equilibrio, e nella possibilità di trasformare un materiale comune attraverso un processo di lavorazione intensivo, che si riconosce la specificità della sua ricerca.

Von Rydingsvard mal sopportava l’approccio teorico e la fredda sensibilità del Minimalismo, tanto da dire una volta al curatore Mark Rosenthal , che organizzò una mostra delle sue opere nel 2018 al Fabric Workshop and Museum di Philadelphia, che «Non c’era sensualità, e non c’era nemmeno umanità».

title_original: Reza Rahadian, Eva Celia and Christine Hakim Talk “The Sea Speaks His Name”, 1998, Political Memory and Finding Truth in Performance
editorial_title_zh: 雷扎·拉哈迪安、伊娃·塞利娅和克里斯蒂娜·哈基姆谈论《The Sea Speaks His Name》、1998年、政治记忆以及在表演中寻找真相
editorial_excerpt_zh: 雷扎·拉哈迪安、伊娃·塞利娅和克里斯蒂娜·哈基姆讨论了《The Sea Speaks His Name》、印尼的政治过去、表演与记忆。雷扎·拉哈迪安、伊娃·塞利娅和克里斯蒂娜·哈基姆谈论《The Sea Speaks His Name》、1998年、政治记忆以及在表演中寻找真相

"url": "https://www.biff.kr/eng/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Busan-2026.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Asian Movie Pulse", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对拉哈迪安而言，这个项目其实在很多年前就已经开始了。大约八年前，为了该书的发布，他就在一部短片中饰演过这个角色，这让他对劳特（Laut）以及他身边的世界有了早期的理解。因此，为长片再次饰演这个角色与其说是从零开始，不如说是重逢一个他已经遇到过的人。至于尽管自己目前的年龄却要饰演一名大学生，拉哈迪安开玩笑说这并不是特别困难，因为在20世纪90年代，“大多数学生”无论如何看起来都明显要老得多。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "塞利娅饰演拉蒂·安贾尼（Rati Anjani），一名参与该运动及其组织的艺术系学生。她在一次抗议活动中遇到了劳特，两人渐渐坠入爱河。塞利娅将这段关系描述为建立在强烈的精神亲密和平等基础之上，两人对未来有着相似的期望，对周围的政治工作也有着共同的理解。由于认识拉哈迪安大约12年，她觉得彼此原有的熟悉感也让这次合作格外自然。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉哈迪安提到了与那个时期相关的一个词组，“cinta bersemi setelah aksi”——在游行之后萌芽的爱情。对他而言，这种政治承诺与浪漫的交织是这个故事中最具人性的方面之一。两个人可以一方面参与由宏大理想驱动的运动，另一方面同时发现与自己怀有同样信念的人。他也特别高兴能再次与塞利娅合作，并形容她是自己一直想要合作的演员。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他对1998年那段时期的记忆虽然碎片化但却很鲜活。拉哈迪安当时还在读小学最后一年，但他记得母亲下班回家告诉他，由于道路和公共交通被阻断，她曾坐着坦克穿过了苏迪曼（Sudirman）地区。他还记得骚乱蔓延到他自己的街区，有人从商店里拿走商品。当时，他并不明白这一切为什么会发生。直到后来，通过书籍、新闻报道以及他对政治日益增长的兴趣，他才开始理解自己童年所目睹的事情的规模。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些记忆帮助他走近劳特，后者的性格比那种刻板印象中高调直言的活动人士更为复杂。拉哈迪安将他形容为沉思且相对安静，同时承载着恐惧与勇气。这种矛盾变得尤为重要，因为劳特正参与一场政治斗争，却未必具备人们可能与运动领袖联系在一起的外向气质。甚至他对组织内另一位资深人物的倾慕，也由于阶层以及他本人对公开面对自己情感的抗拒而保持着克制。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "角色在影片过半时的失踪带来了另一个挑战。拉哈迪安意识到，在角色的银幕实体缺席之后，他的声音必须继续承载劳特的存在。因此，旁白变得至关重要，它不仅仅是情节交代，更是另一种形式的表演。他希望字里行间的情感能够保留角色的存在感，让观众在看不到他之后依然能感受到他的存在。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对塞利娅而言，这种失踪带来的情感后果变得格外苛刻。安贾尼起初拒绝接受劳特遭到绑架，并开始将各种征兆和迷信解释为他可能仍在与自己交流的证据。塞利娅将此描述为一种应对机制，是某人在被悲伤和不确定性压垮时，为自己创造出一种能够在情感上熬过去的替代解释的方式。因此，她的许多戏份与其说是体力上的困难，不如说是心理上的筋疲力尽。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "克里斯蒂娜·哈基姆从另一个方向处理了同样的缺席，她饰演劳特的母亲，一位儿子离开后便再没有回来的摄影师。对哈基姆而言，难点在于刻画一位被迫在没有确切结果的情况下继续生活的母亲。在她看来，这个角色是她职业生涯现阶段所遇到的那些截然不同的女性形象的又一个例证，此前她饰演过包括在《Four Seasons in Java》中扮演的女性等角色。她对年轻导演继续信任她出演高难度角色表达了特别的感激，并认为支持年轻电影人是她作为印尼影坛资深人物的责任之一。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "哈基姆和拉哈迪安已经多次饰演母子，这使得他们建立联系相对容易，尽管角色本身每次都不同。哈基姆认为他是一个“才华横溢的演员”，并觉得他们现有的默契让他们能够专注于适应每个新故事的具体环境，而不必从一开始就刻意制造熟悉感。她还提到了另一个即将合作的项目，他们在其中将再次饰演母子，这说明了同一对银幕搭档如何根据角色的不同发挥出截然不同的效果。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "岁月的增长并没有削弱哈基姆对高难度角色的兴趣。恰恰相反：她说自己现在必须付出比年轻时多五倍甚至十倍的努力。身体上的准备、饮食、专注以及在片场维持足够的精力都需要更强的自律。她拒绝试图永远固守自己年轻时的浪漫角色这一想法，直言时间无法阻挡，演员必须随着生活继续适应。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种适应也意味着积极参与角色的构建。哈基姆谈到了通过身体、灵魂和思想的结合来进行表演。服装、化妆和视觉设计或许能提供物质上的外在，但演员仍然必须找到如何赋予这个外在以灵魂的方法。她很乐意向导演提出源自这一过程的建议，并举例了她在《Four Seasons in Java》中的角色，当时她提议让一只鸡作为陪伴，因为比起更常规的宠物，这更能反映出这个女性孤立的生存状态。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉哈迪安和切利亚将安吉·诺恩的导演风格描述为精准而不死板。导演确切地知道他从一场戏中需要什么，但同时也为演员留出了足够的空间去探索如何达到这一目标。切利亚尤其赞赏他建立的是环境和背景，而不是命令演员去产生某种特定的情绪。拉哈迪安对这种方法的总结甚至更加直接：“安吉从不指导情绪。他指导动机。”他不是要求某人哭泣，而是给他们最终可能会催生泪水的理由。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管如此，制作过程依然要求极高。拉哈迪安记得玉米地里的一场大型夜戏是最困难的戏份之一，涉及庞大的演员阵容、雨水、泥浆，并且一直拍摄到清晨。玉米本身就是专门为了这部制作而种下的，这要求电影制作人等待大约三个月，直到拍摄地准备就绪。其他场景之所以奏效，恰恰是因为制作方拒绝人工扩大空间。例如，一个小型的家庭厨房迫使演员不断四处走动并彼此碰撞，创造了一种亲密感和日常的忙碌感，拉哈迪安觉得这种效果非常棒。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "政治语境不可避免地将对话引向了当代的印尼。拉哈迪安认为，如今的公民空间“正在稍微缩减”，尽管他强调目前的状况仍然比20世纪90年代要好得多。人们可以阅读、批评政府并以过去危险得多的方式公开直言，但新型的恐吓已经出现，包括匿名的网络攻击以及挑起公民之间冲突的企图。方法或许已经变了，但他觉得电影中探讨的一些紧张关系依然具有现实意义。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "与此同时，他对印尼电影本身保持乐观。国际上出现的各种印尼电影作品反映了他所看到的日益多元的产业，该产业愿意通过截然不同的类型和风格来与不同的社会现实进行互动。与此同时，切利亚对于自己重返表演岗位感到由衷的感激。在大约12年前出演她的第一部剧情长片后，她花了大约十年的时间主要专注于音乐，然后才重回电影界。《The Sea Speaks His Name》现在将她带到了她的第一个国际电影节，她对此充满了感激之情。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉哈迪安也在继续平衡表演和导演工作。他目前正在开发他的第二部长片《Casparina》，他此前一直在亚洲创投会（Asian Project Market）上推介该项目。该片基于他自己的家族历史，讲述了一位母亲在围绕1965年的政治动荡期间缺席的故事。他的祖母曾在乌得勒支流亡，并在苏哈托倒台32年后回到印尼，试图与那些在没有她陪伴下长大的孩子们重新建立联系。拉哈迪安作为青少年曾亲历过那次归家之旅，如今他认为这是他接下来想要讲述的故事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "据悉哈基姆将饰演祖母一角，她已经开始推掉其他项目，以便为这个角色做好充分准备。与此同时，切利娅正为一部细节尚不能透露的动作片做准备。他们未来的项目或许会走向截然不同的方向，但《海诉其名》将这三人紧密凝聚在一个依然能引发共鸣的主题周围：个人生活如何承载政治历史，以及当某人突然被带走时，爱、记忆与家庭又是如何顽强延续的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "摘要：雷扎·拉哈迪安、伊娃·切利娅和克里斯蒂娜·哈基姆畅谈政治记忆、表演、失去以及《海诉其名》。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "标签：The Sea Speaks His Name, Reza Rahadian, Eva Celia, Christine Hakim, Yosep Anggi Noen, Leila S. Chudori, Indonesian Cinema, Indonesia, Busan International Film Festival, BIFF, Asian Cinema, 1998 Indonesia, Political Cinema, Asian Project Market, Casparina", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "Reza Rahadian, Eva Celia and Christine Hakim Talk “The Sea Speaks His Name”, 1998, Political Memory and Finding Truth in Performance"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Reza Rahadian, Eva Celia and Christine Hakim discuss “The Sea Speaks His Name”, Indonesia’s political past, acting and memory."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“The Sea Speaks His Name” brings together Reza Rahadian , Eva Celia and Christine Hakim in a story rooted in Indonesia’s political upheaval of the late 1990s, following young activists whose lives, relationships and families are changed by the violence surrounding the period. Based on the work of Leila S. Chudori, the film also marks another collaboration between Rahadian and director Yosep Anggi Noen , while giving Celia one of her first major acting roles after spending much of the previous decade concentrating on music.", "links": [{"text": "Reza Rahadian", "url": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/tag/reza-rahadian/"}, {"text": "Eva Celia", "url": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/tag/eva-celia/"}, {"text": "Christine Hakim", "url": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/tag/christine-hakim/"}, {"text": "Yosep Anggi Noen", "url": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/tag/yosep-anggi-noen/"}]}, {"type": "heading", "text": "The Sea Speaks His Name is screening at Busan International Film Festival", "links": [{"text": "Busan International Film Festival", "url": "https://www.biff.kr/eng/"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://asianmoviepulse.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Busan-2026.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Asian Movie Pulse"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "For Rahadian, the project actually began many years earlier. He had already played the character in a short film made around eight years ago for the launch of the book, giving him an early understanding of Laut and the world around him. Returning to the character for the feature therefore felt less like starting from zero than revisiting someone he had already encountered. As for playing a university student despite his current age, Rahadian joked that this was not particularly difficult since “most of the students” in the 1990s looked considerably older anyway."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Celia plays Rati Anjani, an art student involved in the movement and its organization. She meets Laut during a protest and the two gradually fall in love. Celia describes the relationship as one based strongly on intellectual intimacy and equality, with the pair sharing similar hopes for the future and a common understanding of the political work around them. Having known Rahadian for approximately 12 years, she felt that their existing familiarity also made the collaboration particularly natural."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Rahadian refers to a phrase associated with the period, “cinta bersemi setelah aksi” — love that grows after a demonstration. For him, this mixture of political commitment and romance is one of the most human aspects of the story. Two people can be participating in a movement driven by larger ideals while simultaneously discovering someone with whom they share those same convictions. He was also particularly pleased to work with Celia again, describing her as an actress he had wanted to collaborate with for some time."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "His own memories of the 1998 period are fragmented but vivid. Rahadian was still in his final year of elementary school, but remembers his mother returning from work and telling him that she had travelled through the Sudirman area on a tank because roads and public transportation were blocked. He also remembers unrest reaching his own neighborhood and people taking goods from a store. At the time, he did not understand why any of it was happening. Only later, through books, news reports and his growing interest in politics, did he begin to understand the scale of what he had witnessed as a child."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Those memories helped him approach Laut, whose personality is more complicated than that of the stereotypically vocal activist. Rahadian describes him as contemplative and relatively quiet, carrying fear and courage at the same time. That contradiction became important because Laut is participating in a political struggle while not necessarily possessing the extroverted temperament people might associate with a movement leader. Even his attraction toward another senior figure within the organization remains restrained by hierarchy and his own reluctance to confront his feelings openly."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The character’s disappearance halfway through the film presented another challenge. Rahadian realized that his voice would have to continue carrying Laut’s presence after his physical absence from the screen. Narration consequently became essential, not simply as exposition but as another form of performance. He wanted the emotion behind the words to preserve the character’s presence and allow audiences to continue feeling him even after he was no longer visible."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "For Celia, the emotional consequences of that disappearance become particularly demanding. Anjani initially refuses to accept that Laut has been kidnapped and begins interpreting signs and superstitions as evidence that he may still communicate with her. Celia describes this as a coping mechanism, a way for someone overwhelmed by loss and uncertainty to create an alternative explanation she can emotionally survive. Many of her scenes were therefore less physically difficult than psychologically exhausting."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Christine Hakim approaches the same absence from another direction, playing Laut’s mother, a photographer whose son leaves and simply does not return. For Hakim, the difficulty lies in portraying a parent forced to continue living without certainty. She sees the role as another example of the very different women she has been offered at this stage of her career, following characters including the woman she played in “Four Seasons in Java”. She expressed particular gratitude that younger directors continue trusting her with demanding parts and considers supporting younger filmmakers one of her responsibilities as an established figure in Indonesian cinema."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Hakim and Rahadian have already played mother and son several times, something that makes establishing their connection relatively easy even though the characters themselves are always different. Hakim considers him a “brilliant actor” and feels that their existing chemistry allows them to concentrate on adapting to the specific circumstances of each new story rather than having to manufacture familiarity from the beginning. She also points toward another upcoming project in which they again play mother and son, illustrating how differently the same pairing can function depending on the characters."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Aging has not made Hakim less interested in difficult roles. Quite the opposite: she says she now has to work five or even ten times harder than when she was younger. Physical preparation, diet, concentration and maintaining enough energy on set all require greater discipline. She rejects the idea of trying to remain permanently associated with the romantic roles of her youth, arguing simply that time cannot be stopped and an actor has to continue adapting along with life."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "That adaptation also means participating actively in the construction of a character. Hakim speaks of performance through the combination of body, soul and mind. Costume, makeup and visual design may provide the physical exterior, but an actor must still discover how to give that exterior a soul. She is comfortable offering directors suggestions when they emerge from this process, citing her character in Four Seasons in Java, for whom she proposed having a chicken as a companion because it better reflected the woman’s isolated existence than a more conventional pet would have."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Rahadian and Celia describe Anggi Noen’s directing style as precise without being rigid. The director knows exactly what he needs from a scene, but creates enough space for the actors to explore how to reach it. Celia particularly appreciates that he establishes an environment and context rather than ordering an actor to produce a specific emotion. Rahadian summarizes the method even more directly: Anggi “never directs the feeling. He directs the motive.” Instead of asking someone to cry, he gives them the reason that might eventually produce tears."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The production could nevertheless be demanding. Rahadian remembers a major nighttime sequence in a cornfield as one of the most difficult, involving a large cast, rain, mud and filming into the early hours of the morning. The corn itself had been planted specifically for the production, requiring the filmmakers to wait around three months until the location was ready. Other scenes worked precisely because the production refused to artificially enlarge its spaces. A small family kitchen, for example, forced the actors to constantly move around and bump into one another, creating an intimacy and everyday busyness that Rahadian felt worked beautifully."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The political context inevitably led the conversation toward contemporary Indonesia. Rahadian believes civil space today is “a little bit shrinking”, although he emphasizes that conditions remain considerably better than in the 1990s. People can read, criticize the government and speak openly in ways that were previously far more dangerous, but new forms of intimidation have appeared, including anonymous cyberattacks and attempts to provoke conflict between citizens. article_text:
Reza Rahadian, Eva Celia and Christine Hakim Talk “The Sea Speaks His Name”, 1998, Political Memory and Finding Truth in Performance

Reza Rahadian, Eva Celia and Christine Hakim discuss “The Sea Speaks His Name”, Indonesia’s political past, acting and memory.

“The Sea Speaks His Name” brings together Reza Rahadian , Eva Celia and Christine Hakim in a story rooted in Indonesia’s political upheaval of the late 1990s, following young activists whose lives, relationships and families are changed by the violence surrounding the period. Based on the work of Leila S. Chudori, the film also marks another collaboration between Rahadian and director Yosep Anggi Noen , while giving Celia one of her first major acting roles after spending much of the previous decade concentrating on music.

The Sea Speaks His Name is screening at Busan International Film Festival

For Rahadian, the project actually began many years earlier. He had already played the character in a short film made around eight years ago for the launch of the book, giving him an early understanding of Laut and the world around him. Returning to the character for the feature therefore felt less like starting from zero than revisiting someone he had already encountered. As for playing a university student despite his current age, Rahadian joked that this was not particularly difficult since “most of the students” in the 1990s looked considerably older anyway.

Celia plays Rati Anjani, an art student involved in the movement and its organization. She meets Laut during a protest and the two gradually fall in love. Celia describes the relationship as one based strongly on intellectual intimacy and equality, with the pair sharing similar hopes for the future and a common understanding of the political work around them. Having known Rahadian for approximately 12 years, she felt that their existing familiarity also made the collaboration particularly natural.

Rahadian refers to a phrase associated with the period, “cinta bersemi setelah aksi” — love that grows after a demonstration. For him, this mixture of political commitment and romance is one of the most human aspects of the story. Two people can be participating in a movement driven by larger ideals while simultaneously discovering someone with whom they share those same convictions. He was also particularly pleased to work with Celia again, describing her as an actress he had wanted to collaborate with for some time.

His own memories of the 1998 period are fragmented but vivid. Rahadian was still in his final year of elementary school, but remembers his mother returning from work and telling him that she had travelled through the Sudirman area on a tank because roads and public transportation were blocked. He also remembers unrest reaching his own neighborhood and people taking goods from a store. At the time, he did not understand why any of it was happening. Only later, through books, news reports and his growing interest in politics, did he begin to understand the scale of what he had witnessed as a child.

Those memories helped him approach Laut, whose personality is more complicated than that of the stereotypically vocal activist. Rahadian describes him as contemplative and relatively quiet, carrying fear and courage at the same time. That contradiction became important because Laut is participating in a political struggle while not necessarily possessing the extroverted temperament people might associate with a movement leader. Even his attraction toward another senior figure within the organization remains restrained by hierarchy and his own reluctance to confront his feelings openly.

The character’s disappearance halfway through the film presented another challenge. Rahadian realized that his voice would have to continue carrying Laut’s presence after his physical absence from the screen. Narration consequently became essential, not simply as exposition but as another form of performance. He wanted the emotion behind the words to preserve the character’s presence and allow audiences to continue feeling him even after he was no longer visible.

For Celia, the emotional consequences of that disappearance become particularly demanding. Anjani initially refuses to accept that Laut has been kidnapped and begins interpreting signs and superstitions as evidence that he may still communicate with her. Celia describes this as a coping mechanism, a way for someone overwhelmed by loss and uncertainty to create an alternative explanation she can emotionally survive. Many of her scenes were therefore less physically difficult than psychologically exhausting.

Christine Hakim approaches the same absence from another direction, playing Laut’s mother, a photographer whose son leaves and simply does not return. For Hakim, the difficulty lies in portraying a parent forced to continue living without certainty. She sees the role as another example of the very different women she has been offered at this stage of her career, following characters including the woman she played in “Four Seasons in Java”. She expressed particular gratitude that younger directors continue trusting her with demanding parts and considers supporting younger filmmakers one of her responsibilities as an established figure in Indonesian cinema.

Hakim and Rahadian have already played mother and son several times, something that makes establishing their connection relatively easy even though the characters themselves are always different. Hakim considers him a “brilliant actor” and feels that their existing chemistry allows them to concentrate on adapting to the specific circumstances of each new story rather than having to manufacture familiarity from the beginning. She also points toward another upcoming project in which they again play mother and son, illustrating how differently the same pairing can function depending on the characters.

Aging has not made Hakim less interested in difficult roles. Quite the opposite: she says she now has to work five or even ten times harder than when she was younger. Physical preparation, diet, concentration and maintaining enough energy on set all require greater discipline. She rejects the idea of trying to remain permanently associated with the romantic roles of her youth, arguing simply that time cannot be stopped and an actor has to continue adapting along with life.

That adaptation also means participating actively in the construction of a character. Hakim speaks of performance through the combination of body, soul and mind. Costume, makeup and visual design may provide the physical exterior, but an actor must still discover how to give that exterior a soul. She is comfortable offering directors suggestions when they emerge from this process, citing her character in Four Seasons in Java, for whom she proposed having a chicken as a companion because it better reflected the woman’s isolated existence than a more conventional pet would have.

Rahadian and Celia describe Anggi Noen’s directing style as precise without being rigid. The director knows exactly what he needs from a scene, but creates enough space for the actors to explore how to reach it. Celia particularly appreciates that he establishes an environment and context rather than ordering an actor to produce a specific emotion. Rahadian summarizes the method even more directly: Anggi “never directs the feeling. He directs the motive.” Instead of asking someone to cry, he gives them the reason that might eventually produce tears.

The production could nevertheless be demanding. Rahadian remembers a major nighttime sequence in a cornfield as one of the most difficult, involving a large cast, rain, mud and filming into the early hours of the morning. The corn itself had been planted specifically for the production, requiring the filmmakers to wait around three months until the location was ready. Other scenes worked precisely because the production refused to artificially enlarge its spaces. A small family kitchen, for example, forced the actors to constantly move around and bump into one another, creating an intimacy and everyday busyness that Rahadian felt worked beautifully.

The political context inevitably led the conversation toward contemporary Indonesia. Rahadian believes civil space today is “a little bit shrinking”, although he emphasizes that conditions remain considerably better than in the 1990s. People can read, criticize the government and speak openly in ways that were previously far more dangerous, but new forms of intimidation have appeared, including anonymous cyberattacks and attempts to provoke conflict between citizens. The methods may have changed, but he feels some of the tensions explored in the film remain relevant.

At the same time, he is optimistic about Indonesian cinema itself. The range of Indonesian titles appearing internationally reflects what he sees as an increasingly diverse industry willing to engage with different social realities through very different genres and styles. Celia, meanwhile, is particularly grateful simply to have returned to acting. After her first feature around 12 years ago, she spent roughly a decade concentrating primarily on music before moving back toward cinema. “The Sea Speaks His Name” has now brought her to her first international film festival, something she describes with considerable gratitude.

Rahadian is also continuing to balance acting and directing. He is currently developing his second feature, “Casparina”, which he was pitching at the Asian Project Market. Based on his own family history, the film concerns the absence of a mother during the political upheaval surrounding 1965. His grandmother was exiled in Utrecht and returned to Indonesia 32 years later, after the fall of Suharto, attempting to reconnect with children who had grown up without her. Rahadian witnessed that homecoming himself as a teenager and now considers it the story he wants to tell next.

Hakim is expected to play the grandmother and has already begun turning down other projects so she can prepare properly for the role. Celia, meanwhile, is preparing for an action film whose details she cannot yet reveal. Their future projects may move in very different directions, but “The Sea Speaks His Name” brings all three together around a subject that continues to resonate: how personal lives absorb political history, and how love, memory and family persist even when someone is suddenly removed from them.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 阿伦·索尔金将针对Facebook的调查与扎克伯格应对公众的准备工作进行了对比，但过多的解释削弱了两线作战之间的张力。文章《影评 | 《社交网络之外》（2026）：丑闻早已在信息流中》最先出现在……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "阿伦·索尔金将针对Facebook的调查与扎克伯格应对公众的准备工作进行了对比，但过多的解释削弱了两线作战之间的张力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《社交网络之外》在构思之初就面临着一个挑战：如何让观众投入到一场其影响早已融入日常生活之中的揭秘中。如今同样以导演身份回归的阿伦·索尔金再次涉足《社交网络》的宇宙，将焦点从Facebook的创立转移到了其运作所带来的后果上。这种转变腾出了空间，用来审视该平台的决策、它所行使的权力以及它对公众应尽的责任。然而，影片过分依赖信息本身的影响力，却没有构建出配合其发现所需的必要张力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "叙事跟随记者杰夫·霍维茨（杰瑞米·艾伦·怀特饰）展开，他接触了弗朗西丝·豪根（米基·麦迪逊饰），这名Facebook员工对内部数据所揭露的平台现状感到担忧。这项调查旨在证明，纯粹以盈利为导向的决策如何助长了能够使激进用户走向极端的內容的传播。与此同时，我们看到马克·扎克伯格（杰瑞米·斯特朗饰）正为出席美国国会听证会做准备，反复演练回答问题的方式，以防止公众曝光让危机进一步恶化。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这一前提本身充满前景，一方面突出了让证词和文件真正转化为可验证信息所需的努力，另一方面则展现了为管控这些信息的后果而进行的演讲排练。这两条战线都在处理同一事件的公共版本的构建，每一方都出于不同的利益。索尔金清晰地呈现了这种对立，但对于调查试图证明的内容与这位亿万富翁试图控制的内容之间的冲突，却着墨不多。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "时间线上的来回穿梭试图赋予素材以动感，但单靠这种交替并不能产生影片所力图成为的那种新闻惊悚片所需的紧迫感。调查本身归结为一堆信息的累积，其叙事序列似乎永远处于相同的温度。剧本将豪根描绘成一个内向、在协助调查与保持对Facebook连接人们能力的信念之间纠结的人。然而在镜头前，她有时表现得更为外向，这种矛盾性对她的行为几乎没有产生什么影响。她的冲突最终听起来不过是编剧的小把戏，好让种种内幕一点点透露给霍维茨。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "序幕呈现了一个极端化后果的例子，为这一主题赋予了人性维度。但在此之后，影片便专注于对平台的各种解释，几乎没有将调查的推进与受其运作影响的生活联系起来。就连序幕与其中一位角色的联系在被提及后，也没有实质性地改变谈话和发现的走向。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "难点不仅在于如何切入众所周知的事件，而在于如何将这些信息视为如此震撼的揭秘，以至于仅凭它们就能维持公众的震惊。即使在参与度、Facebook的利润以及用户极端化之间的关系已经确立之后，索尔金仍在冗长地进行解释。这种说教风格使人们能够理解平台的运作方式，却反过来挤占了本该留给这些发现对角色产生的影响的空间。这种滞后感正是源于这种执念：只顾着阐明问题，却不展开描绘它对必须面对它的人而言改变了什么。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在扎克伯格的核心支线中，杰瑞米·斯特朗展现出了极具视觉冲击力的存在感，尽管剧本给他的空间很少，除了重现其外表和习惯之外，无法深入塑造这个角色。这位亿万富翁必须排练如何对影响深远的决策负责，从而将对其行为的问责转化为一场表演问题。这些时刻让人隐约看到了一种权力，它更关心自己将被如何感知，而非它本应为什么负责，但影片对这种可能性的探索非常有限。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《社交网络之外》面临着一场博弈：一方面是将损害公之于众，另一方面是控制人们感知损害的方式。索尔金阐明了该平台的运作机制，但对这场博弈的展开却少之又少，宁愿一遍又一遍地重申这一指控的严重性。这个话题依然具有现实意义；而这部电影在呈现它的方式上却一出生就已过时。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Aaron Sorkin contrapõe a investigação sobre o Facebook à preparação de Zuckerberg para enfrentar o público, mas o excesso de explicações enfraquece a tensão entre as duas frentes.

“ O Outro Lado das Redes ” já foi concebido com o desafio de envolver o espectador numa denúncia cujos efeitos já fazem parte do cotidiano. Agora também como diretor, Aaron Sorkin retorna ao universo de “A Rede Social” , deslocando o foco da criação do Facebook para as consequências do seu funcionamento. Essa mudança abre espaço para examinar decisões da plataforma, o poder que ela exerce e sua responsabilidade perante o público. O filme, porém, confia demais no impacto das informações por si só, sem conceber a tensão necessária para acompanhar sua descoberta.

A narrativa acompanha o jornalista Jeff Horwitz (Jeremy Allen White) em seu contato com Frances Haugen (Mikey Madison), funcionária do Facebook preocupada com o que os dados internos revelam sobre a plataforma. A investigação visa demonstrar como as decisões voltadas puramente à rentabilidade favoreceram a circulação de conteúdos capazes de radicalizar os usuários. Em paralelo, acompanhamos Mark Zuckerberg (Jeremy Strong) se preparando para uma audiência no Congresso dos Estados Unidos, treinando a maneira de responder às perguntas para evitar que a exposição pública agrave ainda mais a crise.

A premissa, por si só, é promissora, destacando, de um lado, o esforço necessário para que depoimentos e documentos se tornem, de fato, informação verificável; e, do outro, a preparação de um discurso que permita administrar as consequências dessa informação. As duas frentes lidam com a construção de uma versão pública dos mesmos acontecimentos, cada uma partindo de interesses diferentes. Sorkin apresenta essa oposição com clareza, mas desenvolve pouco o conflito entre o que a investigação procura demonstrar e o que o bilionário tenta controlar.

As idas e vindas na cronologia procuram dar dinamismo ao material, mas apenas essa alternância não produz a urgência necessária ao thriller jornalístico que o filme se propõe a ser. A investigação se resume a um acúmulo de informações em sequências que parecem estar sempre na mesma temperatura. O texto apresenta Haugen como uma pessoa fechada e dividida entre colaborar com a investigação e preservar sua crença na capacidade do Facebook de conectar pessoas. Em cena, porém, ela por vezes se mostra mais expansiva, e essa ambivalência pouco interfere em suas atitudes. Seu conflito acaba soando como mera traquitana de roteiro para que as revelações sejam entregues a Horwitz aos poucos.

O prólogo apresenta um exemplo das consequências da radicalização, dando uma dimensão humana para o assunto. Depois, porém, o filme se concentra nas explicações sobre a plataforma e pouco relaciona o avanço da investigação às vidas afetadas por seu funcionamento. Mesmo a ligação do prólogo com uma das personagens é mencionada sem alterar significativamente o rumo das conversas e descobertas.

A dificuldade não está simplesmente em abordar acontecimentos conhecidos, mas em tratar essas informações como revelações tão bombásticas que elas, sozinhas, sustentariam o espanto do público. Sorkin prolonga as explicações mesmo depois que a relação entre engajamento, lucro do Facebook e radicalização dos usuários já está estabelecida. O didatismo permite compreender o funcionamento da plataforma, mas passa a ocupar o espaço que falta às implicações das descobertas para os personagens. A sensação de atraso vem dessa insistência em esclarecer o problema sem desenvolver o que ele muda para quem precisa enfrentá-lo.

No núcleo de Zuckerberg, Jeremy Strong surge como uma presença visualmente marcante, embora o material lhe dê pouco espaço para desenvolver o personagem além da reprodução de sua aparência e de seus maneirismos. O bilionário precisa ensaiar como responder por decisões de enorme alcance, convertendo a responsabilização por seus atos em uma questão de desempenho. Esses momentos permitem entrever um poder mais preocupado com a maneira como será percebido do que com aquilo pelo que deveria responder, mas o filme pouco explora essa possibilidade.

“O Outro Lado das Redes” tem diante de si uma disputa entre tornar os danos públicos e controlar a maneira como serão percebidos. Sorkin esclarece o funcionamento da plataforma, mas desenvolve muito pouco essa disputa, preferindo reafirmar a gravidade da denúncia de novo, e de novo. O assunto permanece atual; o filme já nasce datado na maneira de apresentá-lo.

title_original: James Gibson’s Cultural and Spiritual Legacy Lives on in His Sculptures
editorial_title_zh: 詹姆斯·吉布森的文化与精神遗产在雕塑中永存
editorial_excerpt_zh: 詹姆斯·吉布森的职业生涯跨度达60年，是一位备受尊敬的田纳西州教师和雕塑家。如今，他遗产中的240多件雕塑正向收藏家开放购买。

{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在西弗吉尼亚州的这段时间里，吉布森的作品引起了日出查尔斯顿艺术画廊（Charleston Art Gallery at Sunrise）的关注，这是首个为其作品举办展览的大型艺术画廊。吉布森还完成了三项引人注目的委托创作：1966年为南查尔斯顿 FMC 无机化学公司新建的露天中庭花园创作了一座黄铜雕塑喷泉，1967年为莫里斯·哈维学院校园永久安装创作了两座大型黄铜雕塑，以及1968年为改建后的刘易斯雪佛兰（Lewis Chevrolet）汽车经销店入口创作了一座黄铜雕塑。", "links": [{"text": "commissions", "url":
